sources.title: Über
sources.supports: born 1994 in Belarus, grew up in Polesia; Architektur- und Baukolleg Minsk; graphics and printmaking at the Angewandte (diploma 2023); lithography, woodcut, etching, drawing; plants and insects; Klagenfurt since 2023; 2024 Nachwuchspreis Bildende Kunst Kärnten (Wietersdorferpreis)
sources.note: English version: https://katyafrei.com/en/about/ (headline 'About'). The page names the 2024 prize but not that it was the third prize.

sources.title: Biografie
sources.supports: born 1953 in Lienz; school in Klagenfurt with Egon Wucherer; University of Graz; taught at the Handelsakademie Klagenfurt until 2003; studio in Klagenfurt; Šmartno studio 1995; sacred subjects since the 1990s; glass and ceramics; died December 2015
sources.note: The glass cross 'Ich bin das Leben' (1998, St. Johannes Baptista Wölfnitz) is on a separate page of the same site: https://simonitsch-karlheinz.at/werke/uebersicht-einzelobjekte/ich-bin-das-leben

sources.title: bio
sources.supports: born 1970 in Schärding; Academy of Fine Arts Vienna and sports science 1989–1997; École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts Paris 1995; Athens School of Fine Arts 1996–1997; lives and works in Vienna
sources.note: Oil/acrylic and the outdoor panoramas on Crete are not on this page (they are on spittal-drau.at's exhibition page).

sources.title: Über Alfred Scheikl
sources.supports: studies 2012–2016 with Anticevic, Kohl, Fadinger, Langer; master class with Anticevic 2016–2017; chair of the Kunstverein Velden since 2017 and courses there; abstract and fractal elements; works in Klagenfurt

sources.title: Alfred Scheikl – Slikarska razstava
sources.supports: born 1961 in Klagenfurt (Celovec); academy 2012–2016 with Anticevic, Kohl, Fadinger, Langer; chair of the Kunstverein Velden; abstract and fractal elements
sources.note: Exhibition page of Festival Bled 2017 (no publication date on the page).

sources.title: Ausstellung Klaus Zlattinger and Friends
sources.supports: artist, art educator and gallerist; died December 2016; exhibition 'Klaus Zlattinger & Friends' on the 10th anniversary of his death, Impuls Center Seeboden (16 Nov 2026 – 7 Dec 2027)
sources.note: Event page; the vernissage has its own page: https://kultur-impuls.com/events/vernissage-klaus-zlattinger-and-friends-2/

sources.title: Inge Lasser
sources.supports: lives and works in Hermagor; trained with Hoke, Bach and Lüpertz at the Kunstakademie Bad Reichenhall; joined postWERK in 2013; exhibitions in Austria, Germany, Italy, France
sources.note: Member profile post (URL dated 2014-04-05, content updated since). Her role as secretary (Schriftführerin) is on https://postwerk.at/statuten/

sources.title: Curriculum vitae
sources.supports: born 1961 in Villach; University of Applied Arts Vienna 1983–1989; diploma in Ernst Caramelle's master class; Würdigungspreis des Landes Kärnten 2010; lives in Vienna
sources.note: Bilingual page (de/en). The 'Soul Source Records' series is documented under https://uwe-bressnik.info/schallplatten/ssr ; the musician activity since about 2000 is not on the CV page.

sources.title: Der Künstler
sources.supports: born 1927 in Obervellach; teacher; Academy in the afternoons from 1954; artist only from 1964; Schloss Rosenau, then farm near Zwettl; winter studio in the Karl-Marx-Hof; thick paint; fire, sand pits, mountain streams, dancers; died 2015 in Vienna

sources.title: Inge Vavra – Kurzbiografie
sources.supports: born 1942 in Augsburg, grew up in Vienna; 1965 diploma in graphic art and painting, Academy of Fine Arts Vienna; art teacher qualification; exhibiting since 1964; Würdigungspreis des Landes Kärnten 2005; lives and works in Vienna and Krumpendorf
sources.note: PDF short biography from the 2013 Alpen-Adria-Galerie exhibition (Inge Vavra – Helge Hinteregger). The art-in-architecture works (LKH Wolfsberg, Pädagogische Hochschule Klagenfurt) are not in it and were not found on stadtgalerie.net.

sources.title: Biografie
sources.supports: born 1948 in Lunz am See, lives in Vienna; Graphische Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt 1970–1973; Hochschule für angewandte Kunst 1976–1982; professorship at TU Graz, Institute of Contemporary Art, 1995; exhibition list

sources.title: Vita
sources.supports: Landeskonservatorium Klagenfurt 2003–2004; photography 2006; drawing lessons from 2007; woodcut and paper-cut printing since 2016; songwriter since 2010; freelance since 2022, studio and home in Kötschach-Mauthen

sources.title: Über uns
sources.supports: board: Margaretha Maria Bauer vice president and treasurer (Kassier) of the BV Kärnten; the association's gallery in Klagenfurt
sources.note: The site has no working https (certificate for *.a1webhosting.at), so the http URL is the one that loads. That she heads the gallery and her Kunstverein Kärnten / 'schmaler Grat' participation are not on this page.

sources.title: Biografie
sources.supports: born 1905 in Graz; childhood in Carinthia; Academy Vienna 1925–1930, master class Alois Delug; teacher in Vienna and Klosterneuburg; freelance in Klagenfurt from 1946; landscapes in oil, figures; Eduard Kaiser Verlag covers and illustrations; glass windows and mosaics for Carinthian churches; died 1993 in Klagenfurt
sources.note: Bilingual page (de/en). The Kreuzbergl Stations of the Cross mosaics (1959) have their own page: https://karl-bauer.at/kreuzbergl-klagenfurt-kreuzweg-mosaiken/

sources.title: biography
sources.supports: born 1960; Hochschule für Angewandte Kunst under Oswald Oberhuber 1979–1985; professor at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna 1997–2006; commissioner of the Austrian Pavilion, Venice Biennale 2011; lives and works in Vienna
sources.note: Bilingual page (de/en). Birthplace Hall is not on the page.

sources.title: Adi Schmölzer verbindet Kunst und Jazz
sources.supports: artist and architect; studied architecture under Günther Domenig; paints mainly women in motion; large pictures made on the floor; listens to jazz while painting; permanent display at iXart in Spittal

sources.title: Adi Schmölzer stellt in Sachsenburg aus
sources.supports: Upper Carinthian artist; after years of work in Graz and Burgenland returned to Carinthia and lives in Spittal; paints to the rhythm of jazz
sources.note: Published by the Osttiroler Bote (Oberkärnten edition).

sources.title: Über mich/Bio
sources.supports: Freie Akademie Klagenfurt 2013–2017; master class with Luka Anticevic 2018–2020; European Art Academy Trier 2005, 2006; Bad Reichenhall 2011
sources.note: Bilingual page (de/en). Her theme 'dialogue between paper and painting' is on the homepage https://www.inesurach.at/ ; the studio in the Europahaus is not stated on either page.

sources.title: Persönlich
sources.supports: née Juch, born 4 April 1965 in Völkermarkt; lives and works in Kühnsdorf; graduate of the Freie Akademie; master class with Luka Anticevic and Peter Kohl; prize at the Ex Tempore di Grisignana 2012
sources.note: The HTML <title> is the site name only; 'Persönlich' is the menu name of the page. Course instructor at the Kunstverein Velden is not on this page.

sources.title: Slava Mohl
sources.supports: born 1978 in Bosnia, in Austria since 1992; hotel and catering assistant, then office clerk; 2016 master class for painting at the HTBLA Ortweinschule Graz; freelance since; pigment, chalk, paper, canvas
sources.note: Exhibitions (Velden, Wolfsberg, Eisenstadt) are on https://www.slavaart.at/?page_id=69 ; the studio in Deutsch Kaltenbrunn is not stated on the site pages checked.

sources.original: invitation and poster of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia
sources.title: Epische Gemälde – Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos (invitation and poster)
sources.supports: title, artist, poster image 'Endzeit', dates
sources.note: Printed invitation and poster of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia (Stadtgemeinde Spittal an der Drau). Local copies: _360_GALLERIES_AND_TOURS/collection/_galleries/galerie_porcia/2026-09-11-galerie-porcia-ingrid-proeller-epische-gemaelde/poster.pdf and _MATERIAL/gbs Einladung_Epische_Gemaelde.pdf, gbs Plakat_Epische_Gemaelde.pdf (image-only PDFs). No online PDF copy found; spittal-drau.at's exhibition page links none.

sources.title: "Epische Gemälde | Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos"
sources.supports: large formats in the Salamancakeller; archaic to futuristic; Mensch, Natur, Kosmos; 'Wildes Kind', 'Kretische Landschaft', 'Fabel', 'Geburt', 'Endzeit' (boy, octopus), 'Matrix' (cosmonaut as modern Odysseus); Pröller born 1970 in Schärding, Academy Vienna; outdoor studio on Crete; 12 Sep – 24 Oct 2026

sources.title: Neue Ausstellung -Sehnsucht- in Kötschach-Mauthen
sources.supports: stARTup Gallery Kötschach-Mauthen; opening at the Lange Nacht der Museen on 3 Oct 2026; woodcuts and frottages on 'Schmerzliches Verlangen nach dem Unerreichbaren'; open 4 Oct – 31 Dec, Fridays 17–19
sources.note: News list page without single-post URLs; the entry is the first item on the page and will move down as news is added. The 2024 prints show at the gallery is on https://waltherpreiml.at/vita/

sources.title: stARTup gallery
sources.supports: ORF Lange Nacht der Museen programme: vernissage Walther Preiml, mountains of the region from his own perspective, own songs
sources.note: Programme page of the venue; content is replaced for each year's Lange Nacht.

sources.title: Ausstellung „Blinddate der Perspektiven“
sources.supports: graduates of the Freie Akademie der bildenden Künste Kärnten; three positions meeting as a blind date; Impuls Center Seeboden; further works in the Marktgemeindeamt Seeboden; 14 Sep – 11 Nov 2026
sources.note: Event page (no publication date).

sources.title: Blinddate der Perspektiven
sources.supports: kultur.im.puls; graduates of the Freie Akademie; three artistic paths; vernissage 11 Sep 2026 Impuls Center Seeboden; stairwell of the Seeboden municipal office

sources.title: Home
sources.supports: Urach's 'Dialog zwischen Papier und Malerei': paper as material in abstract pictures
sources.note: The facts are on the homepage itself (no separate statement page).

sources.title: über mich
sources.supports: von Heyl: study at the Akademie der Bildenden Künste Kärnten from 2020; process-based painting in mixed media

sources.title: Vita
sources.supports: Bucher-Sakowski: graduate of the Freie Akademie der bildenden Künste Kärnten; 2026 kultur im.puls Seeboden in the exhibition list
sources.note: Her figurative acrylic paintings are shown on https://www.bucher-sakowski.at/malerei/serie-1 ('Werkserie Gegenständlich', mostly 'Acryl auf Leinen').

sources.title: "FRAGIL" Jahresausstellung Kunstverein postWERK
sources.supports: postWERK annual exhibition at the Dinzlschloss; the tender as attention, not weakness; artists from Austria, Germany, Slovenia and Iran; painting, photography, installation, literature, performance; vulnerability, fragile ecosystems, shared future; Triennale IV Kärnten 2026 'schwach • šibko • debole'
sources.note: 'Current exhibition' page of the Dinzlschloss: its content will be replaced by the next exhibition.

sources.title: FRAGIL | Jahresthema 2026
sources.supports: annual theme FRAGIL; members and guest artists; Dinzlschloss Villach; Triennale IV Kärnten 2026; Lange Nacht 3 Oct 2026 with the performance 'Wieso wir uns wiegen' by Christina Clar and Phil Yaeger
sources.note: Date taken from the post URL. The Lange Nacht post is https://postwerk.at/2026/09/10/fragil-orf-lange-nacht-der-museen/

sources.title: Dinzlschloss / Kulturabteilung der Stadt Villach
sources.supports: ORF Lange Nacht der Museen programme: postWERK exhibition 'fragil', artists from four countries; performance 'Wieso wir uns wiegen' with Christina Clar and Phil Yaeger at 19, 20, 21
sources.note: Programme page of the venue; content is replaced for each year's Lange Nacht.

sources.title: Universität
sources.supports: founded 1970; four faculties and 30 institutes; student numbers
sources.note: The page now says more than 13,700 students (the text says more than 13,300). The Institut für Unterrichts- und Schulentwicklung belonging to the Fakultät für Kulturwissenschaften/Bildungswissenschaften is not on this page.

sources.title: Kunstverein
sources.supports: founded 2012; non-profit; annual focus with long-standing members and guest artists; Villach (Galerie Offenes Atelier D.U.Design under Dorothee Unkel until 2015)
sources.note: Dorothee Unkel as honorary president since February 2020 and Barbara Ambrusch-Rapp as chair are on https://postwerk.at/statuten/ ; 'Obfrau bis Jänner 2020: Dorothee Unkel' is on https://postwerk.at/impressum/
